answer.rationale: Write-path p99 degradation began ~30 minutes after the release, a strong temporal correlation consistent with memory_b1 (rollback cleared a prior error spike) and memory_b6 (releases are a known regression source). Read-replica routing (b5) targets read load, not the write path, so it doesn't fit. Failover (b2) and circuit breakers (b4) address infrastructure/partner faults with no evidence here. Adding capacity (b3) helps organic surges but the timing points at the release, and provisioning won't fix a regression. Risk flagged: rolling back during peak settlement writes could lose or conflict with in-flight customer writes if the new build changed write formats — hence verifying b1's archived record for how the prior rollback handled writes before committing. If verification shows write-safety concerns, I would fall back to add_capacity as the lower-risk bridge.
